methodology: Every entry below was produced by one of exactly two methods, recorded per-entry in 'provenance': (1) 'multimodal_visual_read' -- the PDF page was rendered as an image and read directly by Claude (the model authoring this file) via the Read tool's PDF rendering, cross-referenced against printed component labels visible on the page; (2) 'user_verbatim' -- the user directly transcribed table contents in an earlier conversation turn (the five switch-continuity tables), used here as a higher-trust cross-check against the visual read. No OCR, no automated symbol-detection, and no coordinate-extraction tooling was used -- this is a human-grade (Claude-grade) visual read, not an ingestion-pipeline run, and should NOT be mistaken for a preview of ingestion accuracy. Positional descriptions ('sourceRegion') are qualitative (e.g. 'top-left area, inside the BATTERY box') because the PDF has no embedded text layer and no reliable coordinate system was established for this single-page raster scan -- inventing precise pixel/point coordinates was explicitly avoided per task instructions. Every entry lists a 'confidence' of high / medium / low / unresolved; nothing below was guessed to fill a gap -- low-confidence and unresolved entries are marked as such rather than asserted.

confidenceLevels.high: Component's printed text label on the page is unambiguous and directly matches (or trivially maps to) the ground-truth object's displayName/category, with a clearly distinct drawn symbol.
confidenceLevels.medium: Component is visually identifiable and plausibly matched, but the page is dense (overlapping wires, small print in switch tables, or a symbol shared/adjacent to a similar one) such that a second independent reviewer might reasonably disagree on an exact boundary or table cell.
confidenceLevels.low: A plausible match exists but rests on structural inference (e.g. 'this must be the node between X and Y because the ground-truth graph says so') rather than a directly readable label on the page.
confidenceLevels.unresolved: No distinct drawn symbol/label corresponds 1:1 to this ground-truth object on the page; the object is an OEP graph-modeling construct (typically a connector node) that the schematic represents only implicitly, as an unlabeled wire junction or an internal wire-harness connector not broken out as its own box in this particular manual page.

spliceCorrespondence.sourceElement: Solid filled dots ('junction dots') drawn at wire-branch points -- standard factory-wiring-diagram convention for a splice/branch that is not a discrete physical connector
spliceCorrespondence.notes: At the CATEGORY level (medium confidence): the existence of 14 splice nodes in the ground-truth graph is consistent with this page's dense wire-branching pattern and its convention of marking branch points with solid dots. At the INDIVIDUAL level (unresolved / requires_human_annotation for all 14): establishing exactly which of the many dots on the page corresponds to which specific oepNodeId would require either a zoomed, region-by-region re-read cross-referenced dot-by-dot against the graph's own wire endpoint list, or direct human annotation -- this was not attempted here because it risks producing 14 fabricated coordinate guesses, which the task explicitly prohibits. This is flagged as the single largest concrete gap in this mapping and the most valuable target for a future human-annotation pass.

This is reported honestly per the task's explicit 'do not guess' instruction, and is itself a meaningful finding: OEP's graph model represents wiring-harness structure (connectors, splices) at a finer grain than this particular factory diagram page draws it, which is exactly the kind of gap a future ingestion benchmark needs to be able to measure and report rather than silently paper over.
